A-I 285.description: Combines multidisciplinary AI solution projects, professional communication and internship preparation without establishing one primary subject.

A-I 495.description: Supervised field experience or internship has an individually selected subject; the generic description does not establish its discipline.

CMPSC 432.description: Centers on exploratory data-mining algorithms, including clustering, association and anomaly detection; programming implements these methods.

CMPSC 441.description: Centers on AI search, knowledge representation, planning, learning and neural networks.

CMPSC 446.description: Centers on pattern discovery, decision-tree and ensemble classification, clustering and graph mining.

DS 220.description: Compares relational, key-value, column, vector and graph databases and distributed storage for data management.

DS 300.description: Centers on techniques, processes and design principles for protecting privacy and security of data systems.

DS 320.description: Centers on designing, implementing and evaluating integration of heterogeneous data using relational and other data representations.

DS 330.description: Combines interactive visual-interface design, computational analytics and human analytical reasoning; no single subject predominates.

DS 402.description: Each repeatable offering studies a selected emerging data-science innovation; the generic description does not establish a stable primary subject.

DS 420.description: Combines statistical network models and properties with community detection, classification and embedding methods.

DS 441.description: Centers on information storage and retrieval systems, databases, web search and information organization.

EE 454.description: Computer-vision methods cover segmentation, feature extraction, stereo/depth, motion and object recognition.

EE 483.description: Centers on physical robotics motion/control and components such as actuators and sensors; the description does not assert AI methods.

MATH 425.description: Centers on operations-research model formulation and mathematical allocation and inventory problems.

MATH 429.description: Studies metric/topological spaces, separation, compactness, connectedness and the fundamental group.

MATH 430.description: Studies vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, eigenvalues and linear equations.

MATH 448.description: Centers on mathematical finance models for pricing, hedging and optimization, including binomial and Black-Scholes models.

MATH 452.description: Centers on deep neural networks, convolutional models, training algorithms and their mathematical analysis; numerical methods support these AI techniques.

MATH 455.description: Studies numerical root finding, interpolation, quadrature and linear-system methods.

MATH 486.description: Studies mathematical game-theory models, theorems and optimal-strategy methods.

STAT 380.description: Centers on statistical reasoning and inference through data case studies; programming and data preparation support the statistical analysis.

STAT 462.description: Studies linear/multiple/nonlinear regression, correlation and model selection.

STAT 463.description: Studies time-series models, parameter estimation, forecasting, diagnostics and spectral methods.

STAT 464.description: Studies nonparametric tests, chi-square methods and correlation for nominal and ordinal data.

IST 140.description: Centers on program construction, problem solving, data representations, testing and debugging.

IST 220.description: Centers on network transmission, routing, protocols, internetworking hardware, security and communications management.

IST 240.description: Centers on programming-language paradigms, formal specification, types, bindings, control structures and processors.

IST 242.description: Centers on object-oriented programming, data structures, algorithms, application architectures and design patterns.

IST 250.description: Combines visual/information design and evaluation of websites with practical construction; no single primary subject is established.

IST 256.description: Centers on web programming in HTML/CSS/JavaScript, APIs and application-development frameworks.

ETI 300W.description: Combines enterprise cloud infrastructure and development workflows with technical documentation and communication as explicit goals.

ETI 301.description: Centers on theories of work and organization and analysis of how IT changes organizational processes and information flows.

ETI 302.description: Centers on professional IT project management: scope, planning, budget, schedule, quality and organizational change.

ETI 435.description: Centers on organizational use and governance of analytics, return on investment, talent and enterprise performance.

ETI 461.description: Centers on database administration, tuning, transactions, concurrency, recovery, query optimization, distributed databases and security.

CYBER 100.description: Introduces computing-system architecture and operation; computing theory supports system literacy.

CYBER 262.description: Hands-on network and host defense includes firewalls, intrusion detection and penetration testing.

SRA 111.description: Explicitly combines technical information security with legal/social analysis and risk assessment across cyber and physical threats.

PSYCH 100.description: Introduces empirical psychological science of behavior, cognition, development and physiological processes; this is psychology domain knowledge, not AI methods.

PSYCH 221.description: Centers on social influence, attitudes, persuasion, conformity, culture, prejudice and interpersonal behavior.

PSYCH 253.description: Studies sensory coding, visual/auditory perception and empirical methods of perceptual psychology.

PSYCH 260.description: Centers on nervous-system anatomy and physiology and their biological relationship to behavior and mental processes.

PSYCH 413.description: The published description identifies psychological development of reasoning, perception and language.

PSYCH 425.description: Studies and critiques psychological theories of emotional experience, understanding and expression.

PSYCH 426.description: Studies cognitive psychology of language development, impairment and bilingualism; this is empirical cognition rather than generic language instruction.

PSYCH 451.description: Studies human motor learning, planning and control through cognitive psychology and physiological evidence; robotics is a related application, not the primary method.

PSYCH 452.description: Studies learning and memory through animal and human experiments; it does not describe machine learning.

PSYCH 455.description: Studies neural bases of cognition with neuroanatomy, functional imaging and behavioral experiments.

PSYCH 458.description: The published description identifies concepts and methods of human cognitive visual-spatial processing.
